Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 103, verse 1–3:

(p-333) Surat al-ʿAṣr

Meccan, though in one of the two narrations from Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah it is Medinan.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿By time (al-ʿaṣr)﴾. This is an oath, and concerning it there are two opinions:

The first: that al-ʿaṣr is the age (al-dahr). This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Zayd ibn Aslam.

The second: that it is the late afternoon, what lies between the decline of the sun and its setting. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah, and from it is the saying of the poet:

"Set out with us in the afternoon, O ʿAmr, for the afternoon has grown short, and in the first journey (rawhah) lie the spoil and the reward."

He singled it out for the oath because in it are the conclusions of deeds.

It may also bear a third meaning: that it refers to the age of the Messenger (ﷺ), because of its excellence through the renewal of prophethood in it.

And there is a fourth: that it intends the afternoon prayer (ṣalat al-ʿaṣr), which is the middle prayer (al-ṣalah al-wusta), because it is the most excellent of the prayers. This was said by Muqatil.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. By "mankind" is meant the category of people.

Concerning loss (al-khusr) there are four aspects:(p-334)

The first: it is in destruction. This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: it is in evil. This was said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

The third: it is in deficiency. This was said by Ibn Shajarah.

The fourth: it is in punishment. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the consequence of their affair was loss (khusran)﴾. ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite it: "By time, and the calamities of the age, indeed mankind is in loss, and indeed he is in it until the end of the age."

﴿Except those who have believed and done righteous deeds and enjoined one another to truth﴾. Regarding "the truth" (al-haqq) there are three interpretations: The first: that it is monotheism (al-tawhid). This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: that it is the Qur'an. This was said by Qatadah.

The third: that it is Allah. This was said by al-Suddi.

It may also bear a fourth meaning: that one counsels those he leaves behind, at the approach of death, that they must not die except as Muslims.

﴿And enjoined one another to patience﴾. In it there are two aspects:

The first: patience in obedience to Allah. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: patience in what Allah has made obligatory. This was said by Hisham ibn Hassan.

It may bear a third interpretation: patience in refraining from what is forbidden and in not following desires.
